To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the 02+ Hoyle state is a strongly bound state of three α particles, whose properties are well described by a simple α cluster model, and that its structure can be described as a system oscillating between the 0s ground-state-like configuration with a small probability of 0.11 and the chain-like configuration with a larger probability of 0 9.

the Hoyle resonance in 12C is a strongly bound state with a small width, the transition radius to the ground-state-like 01+ configuration is large (≈3 fm), and the Hoyle resonance structure is described as an oscillating system of three alpha particles.

the α-cluster model, which has no free parameters and is based on the α-α potential determined from the α-α phase-shift analysis, describes the 02+-state energy, width, transition matrix element, root-mean-square radius, and structure in an excellent agreement with the experimental results.

the study of the properties of the 12 C(0 ^{2} ^{+} ) state in terms of the three-α cluster model.
the development of a consistent description of the 02+(12C) state within a microscopic α cluster model.
the development of a microscopic description of the Hoyle state, and its application to the description of the 2+ → 1+ monopole transitions.

the Hoyle 12C resonance is a genuine α cluster state.
the Hoyle state is an α-cluster state.
the Hoyle resonance can be described in a very consistent and accurate manner by the α-cluster model.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the 02+ resonance is a very special case, which is described by a simple α-cluster model with an extremely small α-α scattering length, which is the only one of its kind.
